newsitem.title: USA: Electric cars safer than gasoline-powered -- study.
newsitem.headline: Electric cars safer than gasoline-powered -- study.

text.p: Electric cars are significantly safer than gasoline-powered cars and could prevent thousands of deaths and serious injuries annually, a technology assessment organization said Wednesday.

Electric vehicles are safer in nine of 11 safety areas including fires, toxic fumes and rollovers, said the International Center for Technology Assessment, which described itself as a public interest group not funded by industries.
The Washington-based group also said safety considerations linked with the electric vehicle have been exaggerated, such as electric shock, hydrogen gassing and electrolyte spillage.

For electric shock, the report said gasoline-powered cars require more voltage to keep combustion going than an EV battery pack. It said the high-voltage circuit in the EV is self-contained and isolated from the passenger compartment and from the vehicle chassis.

On hydrogen gassing, the report said the three top EV batteries do not release hydrogen gas as part of the chemical process in normal operation. In stressful conditions that could lead to a build-up of hydrogen gas, the report said venting features would ensure that the battery did not become a "powerful bomb."
The report said the amount of electrolytes that could leak from batteries and produce burns "has been minimized to the point of providing EV users extreme safety."
The configuration of the EV battery "virtually eliminates the risk of exposure to toxic and hazardous materials during normal operating conditions," the report said.
